matches.rationale: No finding identifies the inconsistency between Figure 6(b) table metrics and the learning curves in Figure 6(a). Finding 5 concerns a cross-section discrepancy between the main figure and the appendix, not the table-vs-plot inflation within one figure.

Finding 2 explicitly flags a sign error in the f^{return} definition in Section 3.1, showing it contradicts the stated goal of encouraging better-than-average actions. This captures the same sign/ambiguity issue described in the ground truth.
No finding mentions the undisclosed hyperparameter p values and the resulting unfair comparison due to selective reporting. Finding 6 discusses baseline hyperparameter defaults, not the missing p.

Finding 4 directly matches the overstatement in the abstract, quoting claims about completely eliminating sample inefficiency and solving instability, which is the exact claim_interpretation_distortion described.
No finding addresses the suspect citation 'Deng et al., 2025' in Related Work. Finding 1 concerns a different fabricated citation (Kumar et al. 2024) in a different section.
No finding discusses the absence of ethical or societal impact discussion for the RLHF toxicity mitigation experiment. The findings do not cover ethical_integrity_omission.

No finding captures the marketing-style exaggerated language in the Introduction. Finding 4 covers exaggerated claims in the Abstract, but not the rhetorical manipulation specifically in the Introduction.

Finding 3 identifies the contradiction about the reference policy being fixed versus dynamic in Section 3.1 and the mismatch in buffer data collection, which is the same context_misalignment_incoherence described in the ground truth.

No finding mentions the selectively cropped y-axes or omitted early rounds in Figure 6(a) that visually exaggerate performance. The evidence_data_integrity issues about visual encoding are not detected.

No finding addresses the asymmetric experimental design where IIF benefits from per-environment p tuning while baselines are not similarly optimized. Finding 6 covers misrepresentation of baseline hyperparameters, not this asymmetry.
No finding points out the wide confidence intervals and cherry-picked claims of consistent improvement. The claim_interpretation_distortion regarding statistical robustness is not matched.
No finding mentions the missing learning rate in the influence score definition or the inconsistent use of θ_j^{(k)}. The method_logic_consistency issue in the TracIn adaptation is undetected.
No finding reports the omission of negative results or failure to disclose environments where IIF performed worse than baselines. This evidence_data_integrity issue is not captured.

No finding identifies the misattributed claim that f^{return} is structurally equivalent to REINFORCE with a baseline as described in the cited Sutton and Barto section. This reference_background_fabrication is not detected.

No finding highlights the contradiction between the 'negligible overhead' claim in Section 5.1 and the substantial computational cost shown in Appendix B.9 for influence calculation. The context_misalignment_incoherence is unmatched.
